title: Rub out a wrong pencil answer on a loose worksheet with an eraser, holding the sheet down with the other hand
instruction: Rub out the wrong answer on the worksheet (7 x 8 = 54) with the eraser without rubbing out any of the other answers, then put the eraser down.
context: Rubbing out a wrong pencil answer is something every student does. An eraser grips paper far better than a single sheet grips a desk (about 1.0 against 0.45), so an eraser rubbed on a sheet nobody holds carries the sheet with it instead of sliding over the graphite, and a real sheet slides and creases. An art guide: "Always erase in one direction while holding the paper firmly behind your erasing hand. This prevents the paper from buckling or creasing." So one hand presses the loose 5 g sheet to the desk beside the answer, firmly enough that it neither slides nor turns about that hand, while the other rubs the eraser's 13 x 23 mm end back and forth over a 10 mm tall answer box with the other answers 6 mm above and below it, pressing hard enough to erase and with strokes long enough to break the eraser's grip on the paper, without drifting onto them.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table top. (1) Worksheet, loose: one sheet of A4 80 g/m2 paper (21.0 x 29.7 cm, 5.0 g), long side along y, x 10.0 to 31.0, y -12.85 to 16.85. Printed: a title bar, a name line and five sums (7x5=, 7x6=, 7x8=, 7x9=, 7x7=) in rows 16 mm apart at x 23.7, 22.1, 20.5, 18.9, 17.3, each followed by a printed 30 x 10 mm answer box (middles at y -10.0). Pencilled (HB graphite, two digits 7 mm tall) in the boxes: 35, 42, 54, 63, 49; the wrong one, 54, is in the middle row (x 20.5). (2) Eraser, loose: white vinyl block 65 x 23 x 13 mm (Staedtler Mars plastic 526 50 size) in its blue card sleeve, 25 g, standing on its 23 x 13 mm end on the desk at x 17.0, y -17.5, its 13 mm side along x. Both arms at the ready pose, grippers open. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Read every 50 ms step: the sheet's and the eraser's poses, the eraser's contact force on the sheet (PhysX) and each finger's collision-hull points. Each pencilled answer is a set of 1 mm grid cells along its strokes (37 for the wrong answer, 147 for the other four). A cell is rubbed while the eraser's end face covers it, touching the paper there (within 0.3 mm), with the eraser pressing on the sheet at 1 N or more, by how far the face slides over the sheet that step; a cell of the wrong answer is erased after 60 mm of rubbing, a cell of another answer is damaged after 10 mm. 0 for the rest of the run once more than 5% of the other answers' cells are damaged. Where the sheet ends up is not scored (a sheet that travels with the eraser is simply not erased). Otherwise 0.6 x the fraction of the wrong answer erased; 0.75 when at least 90% is erased; 1.0 when at least 90% is erased and the eraser is put down (lowest point within 3 mm of the desk or the sheet), let go (every finger point of both grippers 2 cm or more from it) and still (under 1 mm) for 1 s. Doing nothing scores 0. Real trial: photos of the answer boxes before and after through a transparent 1 mm grid count the wrong answer's cells still showing graphite and the other answers' cells lightened; the video shows the eraser put down and let go.
reset_notes: Lay a fresh printed sheet with the five answers pencilled in (HB, ordinary writing pressure) in place against two strips of tape on the desk at its left and near edges, photograph the answer boxes, and stand the eraser on its end at its place (brush the crumbs off the desk). In simulation each trial starts afresh.
fidelity: Rigid bodies (PhysX), 20 Hz. The sheet is a rigid 0.3 mm plate (real paper 0.1 mm) that slides and turns but does not bend or crease (creasing is not scored). Graphite is not simulated: 1 mm cells are erased by a rule (60 mm of rubbing at 1 N or more, an estimate) and shown by visual marks. Friction estimates: eraser on paper 1.0/0.9, paper on desk 0.45/0.40. The eraser's end meets the paper on a compliant contact (20 N/mm).
scores: Dream-1 run: 0 (the right gripper went to the standing eraser again and again but never took it; the left arm stayed back; nothing rubbed out); demo: 1.0
